claims.claim: detection.kql is plausibly valid Advanced Hunting KQL
claims.evidence: Syntax looks sound: parentheses balanced (34/34), brackets 2/2; real DeviceNetworkEvents columns (InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName/ProductName, RemoteUrl, etc.); array_sort_asc/array_slice/series_subtract/series_stats_dynamic chain is valid; arg_min(Timestamp, ReportId) yields Timestamp and ReportId columns; ipv4_is_in_any_range with a dynamic array is guarded by array_length. BUT line 20 'let LookbackWindow = 4h' and line 36 '| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackWindow)' is exactly the self-inflicted Timestamp filter the task warned about: the platform already bounds the run on ingestion_time() over 4 h, so events ingested late (Timestamp older than 4 h at run time) are silently dropped by this rule. The notes (line 14) present 'ago(4h)' as the intended lookback, so this is a design misunderstanding, not a typo. Secondary: rarity is computed after the ProcessAllowlist exclusion; Epochs list capped at 5000 means interval stats are computed on a truncated sample for very chatty pairs (the notes acknowledge this at line 44).

claims.claim: Using arg_min (first event) as the Timestamp/ReportId key makes successive hourly runs return the same key so XDR de-duplicates
claims.evidence: Plausible given platform dedup across overlapping lookbacks, but unverifiable from outputs; the notes themselves hedge (line 41: 'If XDR is not de-duplicating ... switch arg_min to arg_max'). Flagged as unverified rather than wrong.

claims.claim: The sensor itself (MsSense.exe etc.) would be the top result without the process allowlist
claims.evidence: Reasonable but not demonstrable from outputs; no tenant data or transcript.

suggestions.assertion: promotion-notes.md names MDE network telemetry sampling/throttling or shared destinations (CDNs, Windows Update, telemetry endpoints) as a source of false negatives/positives
suggestions.reason: The 'or shared destinations' branch is satisfied by any FP list that mentions 'CDN' or 'telemetry' (runs B and C pass this way without ever mentioning MDE sampling/throttling). The platform fact the eval cares about (throttled network telemetry => false negatives) is only checked when the run happens to choose that branch; consider making the throttling/FN statement its own assertion.

suggestions.assertion: promotion-notes.md includes a post-deployment check such as the first-run 30-day scan noise burst, an expected volume, or a scheduled review
suggestions.reason: 'A post-deployment check such as ...' passes any 'what to watch' section. Run C passes with no mention of the first-run 30-day scan, no numeric expected volume and no scheduled review date, only generic 'watch volume in the first 24-48h'. Consider requiring the 30-day first-run scan specifically, since it is the one platform behaviour that will surprise the operator.

suggestions.assertion: promotion-notes.md addresses alert volume and deduplication (the 150-alerts-per-run cap, platform dedup, or aggregating to one row per device/destination)
suggestions.reason: Run C passes via 'platform dedup / one row per device-destination' without mentioning the 150-alerts-per-run cap at all; the cap is the operationally important fact and could be a separate assertion.

No assertion checks for a self-inflicted 'Timestamp > ago(4h)' filter in detection.kql. Run C has exactly this (let LookbackWindow = 4h; where Timestamp > ago(LookbackWindow)), which drops late-arriving events that the ingestion_time()-based lookback would have included, yet it passes all 8 assertions. This is the single most discriminating XDR-specific mistake and should be asserted on (negative check).

No assertion checks that the hunt's 'Hours > 12' span condition was rescaled rather than copied. A run that kept 'Hours > 12' inside a 4 h lookback would be structurally unsatisfiable (never fires) but could still pass assertions 1-4 as written.

No assertion checks that the prevalence (Devices <= N) count is computed over the unfiltered population rather than after process/allowlist exclusions. Run C computes rarity after excluding sensor processes, which can make a shared destination look rare; run B explicitly avoids this. The difference is uncaught.

eval_feedback.overall: C passes all 8 assertions, yet it contains the one XDR-specific mistake (self-inflicted Timestamp > ago(4h)) that the eval's platform facts single out, omits the 150-alert cap, the 30-day first-run scan and MDE throttling, and still scores 8/8. The assertion set is not discriminating enough on the platform-contract points; see suggestions.
